description:
The HTTP search endpoint never returns matches from issue records in a repository with the default `.jit` data directory. It searches only linked documents, so a query for text that appears in an issue title or description returns no issue hits.

## Background

`search` in `crates/server/src/routes.rs` (around lines 280-330) runs ripgrep from the worktree root. When the data root is nested in the worktree (the default `.jit`), it adds the glob `.jit/issues/*.json` to the linked document paths. ripgrep skips hidden directories unless `--hidden` is passed, so the glob matches no file under `.jit/`. The separate data-root search that uses the glob `issues/*.json` runs only when the data root is outside the worktree.

Reproduction against a release build, in a fresh repository:

```sh
jit init && jit issue create --title Hello
jit-server --bind 127.0.0.1:38917 &
curl -s '127.0.0.1:38917/api/search?q=Hello'
# 200 with no issue-file matches
rg --glob '.jit/issues/*.json' Hello .            # no output
rg --hidden --glob '.jit/issues/*.json' Hello .   # matches the issue file
```

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: With the default nested `.jit` data directory, a search request for text in an issue's title or description returns a match from that issue's record.
- [hard] REQ-02: Issue-record matches are returned the same way whether the data directory is nested in the worktree or outside it.
- [hard] REQ-03: Linked-document matches are still returned, and files outside issue records and linked documents are still excluded.
- [hard] REQ-04: A regression test serves a search over a repository with a nested `.jit` and asserts that an issue-record match is returned.

## Notes

Found while verifying the release-build reproductions of the audit correctness epic. The core search's argv handling is already correct; this defect is in which files the server route asks it to search.
title: Search endpoint returns no issue matches for the default nested data directory
